reasoning_traces.think:
The concept of immanent expectation arises from experimental manipulation of sensory features within fixed spatial mazes. Animals exhibit disruption when exposed to novel sensory conditions—such as new wall textures or odors—while maintaining unchanged geometry. This suggests an internal model encoding expected sensory outcomes per spatial configuration. The disruption manifests as increased exploration and delayed decision-making, followed by readjustment. These behaviors imply a dynamic Bayesian updating process where prior expectations are revised upon sensory mismatch. The sensory disruption index captures the degree of deviation from expectation, while behavioral readjustment time reflects the system's capacity to recover. Together, these primitives define a cognitive architecture wherein expectation is not static but continuously refined through trial-and-error interaction with environmental cues.
